issues.t: Engine stalls or shuts off while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out with little or no warning, often at low speed or while coasting. Steering and brakes suddenly take much more effort, and the car may restart and stall again.
issues.why: Stalling is the most common engine complaint filed with NHTSA for the Verano, especially for 2012 and 2013. No single cause has been confirmed; dealers often can't reproduce it, and some cases were tied to valve timing faults or low oil.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the oil level, then have stored trouble codes read right away. Ask the dealer to check for updates and bulletins, and file a report with NHTSA.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: The oil level drops a quart or more between changes, sometimes with blue smoke from the tailpipe, a ticking valvetrain when low, or a check engine light. The oil-life monitor does not warn you about a low level.
issues.why: On the 2.4L engine, oil gets past the piston rings and is burned. GM issued a bulletin telling dealers to run an oil consumption test and replace the pistons and rings when use is too high.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every fill-up and keep it full; running low can ruin the engine and the timing chain. Ask a Buick dealer for an oil consumption test under bulletin 13-06-01-003 and keep records of every quart you add.

issues.t: Plugged crankcase vent causes oil use and leaks
issues.sym: Rising oil consumption, oil seeping from seals, or a check engine light, often worse in cold weather.
issues.why: A small crankcase vent (PCV) opening in the intake manifold can freeze or clog. Pressure then builds inside the engine and pushes oil past seals and into the intake. GM covered this under special coverage 14882.
issues.next: Ask a Buick dealer whether your VIN is listed under special coverage 14882. If oil use is high, have the PCV system checked before any bigger engine repair.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch and rattle
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine at start-up or idle, a check engine light, misfires or rough running. In bad cases the engine stalls or won't run.
issues.why: The 2.4L uses a timing chain with a tensioner and guides. Low or worn oil speeds up wear, the chain stretches, and timing drifts. This is an interference engine, so a chain that jumps can damage valves.
issues.next: Don't ignore a new rattle or timing-related codes. Get it checked soon, keep the oil full and fresh, and replace the chain, guides and tensioner together.

issues.t: Check engine light from camshaft timing solenoid
issues.sym: Check engine light with camshaft timing codes such as P0010 or P0014, sometimes with hesitation, rough idle or stalling.
issues.why: The solenoids that control the variable valve timing can stick or fail, and dirty or low oil makes it worse. Some owners found the light came back after a part swap because the real cause was oil or the timing chain.
issues.next: Check the oil level first. Have the codes read; a solenoid is a modest repair, but if the light returns, ask the shop to check timing chain stretch and oil condition.

issues.t: Coolant leak from water pump, pipes or radiator
issues.sym: Low coolant warnings, a sweet smell, drips under the front of the car, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: Owners report leaking water pumps, coolant pipes and radiators on the 2.4L, some under 60,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the coolant level with the engine cold. If you are losing coolant, have the system pressure tested soon. Stop driving if the gauge goes toward hot.

issues.t: Carbon buildup causes rough idle and misfires
issues.sym: Rough idle, stumbling or hesitation, misfire codes and a slow loss of power, usually after 80,000 miles.
issues.why: Both Verano engines are direct injected, so fuel never washes the intake valves. Oil vapor from the crankcase bakes onto them over time.
issues.next: Have misfires diagnosed so coils and plugs are ruled out first. If carbon is the cause, a walnut-blast valve cleaning usually restores smooth running.

issues.t: Steering sticks or feels notchy near center
issues.sym: The steering feels sticky or catches slightly when making small corrections, often after a long highway drive.
issues.why: The electric power steering gear can develop a stick-slip feel. GM covered it under special coverage 14232.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Ask a Buick dealer whether your car qualifies for special coverage 14232. Until it is fixed, keep both hands on the wheel and allow extra space on the highway.

issues.t: Clicking, clunking or shudder when shifting
issues.sym: A click you can feel through the floor when the car shifts from 1st to 2nd, a clunk under your feet, grinding, or a shudder at 10–20 mph.
issues.why: Owners of the 6-speed automatic report these feelings, mostly at low speed and in the cold. Dealers often find no fault, and no single fix has been confirmed.
issues.next: Check the transmission for leaks and have codes read. Ask the dealer to check for software updates and bulletins, and take a test drive with the technician so they feel what you feel.

issues.t: Clear coat peeling
issues.sym: The shiny top layer of paint turns cloudy, flakes or peels, often on the roof, hood and trunk.
issues.why: Clear coat failure is the most reported body problem for 2013 and 2014 Veranos, usually showing up around 45,000–55,000 miles.
issues.next: Take photos and ask a Buick dealer about goodwill help, especially on a low-mileage car. Otherwise, repainting the affected panels is the only lasting fix.

issues.t: Heater or A/C works only some of the time
issues.sym: Heat or A/C comes and goes, blows the wrong temperature, or the blower works only sometimes. The defroster may blow cold and the windows fog.
issues.why: Owners report intermittent climate control faults that dealers struggle to find. Possible causes include the blower, temperature door actuators and climate controls.
issues.next: Note when it happens and which settings you use. If the defroster can't clear the windshield, don't drive until it can. Ask the shop to check the blower circuit and door actuators while the fault is happening.

issues.t: Battery drains and car won't start
issues.sym: The car is dead after sitting a day or more, with no crank or a slow crank, sometimes even after a new battery.
issues.why: Something keeps drawing power with the car off, or the battery is weak. GM published a bulletin on diagnosing parasitic drain on these cars.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system load-tested. If the battery is good, ask for a parasitic draw test to find the circuit that stays awake.

issues.t: Blind spot modules fail and set many warnings
issues.sym: Side blind zone alert stops working, or a cluster of warnings appears at once, such as side detection, parking assist and other messages.
issues.why: The side detection modules sit low at the rear corners where water and salt reach them. Owners report failed modules setting many warnings.
issues.next: Have codes read to confirm which module failed. A used or rebuilt module, or simply disabling the feature, are options besides a new one. Check your mirrors carefully until it is fixed.

issues.t: Check engine light and trouble filling the gas tank
issues.sym: The pump nozzle keeps clicking off when you fill up, and the check engine light comes on.
issues.why: A fault in the evaporative emissions (EVAP) system, which vents fuel vapor from the tank, can block air from escaping while you refuel.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap is tight, then have the codes read. A smoke test will find the faulty valve or hose.

issues.t: Windshield fogs with heavy moisture
issues.sym: Moisture builds up on the inside of the windshield and is hard to clear.
issues.why: Owners report excessive interior moisture. Common causes are the system stuck on recirculation, a wet cabin from a leak, or a clogged A/C drain.
issues.next: Use fresh-air mode with A/C on and defrost. Check the carpets for wetness and have the A/C drain and door seals checked. Don't drive if you can't see clearly.

issues.t: Parking brake warning light from a failed module or switch
issues.sym: The parking brake warning comes on and the electric parking brake may not work properly.
issues.why: Owners report a failed parking brake control module or switch, sometimes with wiring damage.
issues.next: Block the wheels or park in gear on hills until it is repaired. Have the parking brake codes read before replacing parts.

issues.t: Drive belt or tensioner noise
issues.sym: A squeal, chirp or rattle from the front of the engine that may change with engine speed.
issues.why: A worn serpentine belt or a weak belt tensioner lets the belt slip or chatter. An owner of a 2.0L turbo had both replaced under 20,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the belt and tensioner inspected. If the belt breaks, the alternator stops charging and the battery will soon go flat, so don't wait long.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not deploy (recalls)
issues.sym: Often no symptom. The airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: A shorting bar in the steering wheel airbag coil can touch the terminals, so the driver's front airbag may not deploy in a crash. Covered by recalls 12V-522, 13V-023 and 14V-300.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and have the dealer replace the coil for free if it hasn't been done.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can explode (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. In a crash the inflator may burst and throw metal pieces.
issues.why: A manufacturing defect in some driver airbag inflators. Covered by recall 23V-516.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls right away and book the free replacement.

issues.t: Roof-rail side airbag inflator can rupture (recalls)
issues.sym: No warning sign. In a crash the side curtain airbag may only partly inflate and throw metal pieces.
issues.why: A weld on the roof-rail airbag inflator can fail. Covered by recalls 23V-674, 23V-870 and 25V-764.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and have the free airbag module replacement done as soon as parts are available.

issues.t: Key can come out when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: You can pull the key out while the shifter isn't fully in Park, and the car can roll away after you get out.
issues.why: A part in the key cylinder housing can let the key out too early. Recall 16V-502 covers 2013–2014 and 2016–2017 Veranos; carcomplaints lists no recall for 2015.
issues.next: Always confirm the shifter is in Park and set the parking brake. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls for the free fix.

issues.t: Shift cable can disconnect (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter moves but the gear doesn't change, or the display shows Park when the car isn't in Park.
issues.why: The shift cable adjuster can come loose from the shift lever. Covered by recall 14V-092.
issues.next: If the shifter feels loose or the gear doesn't match, set the parking brake and don't drive. Check your VIN for the free repair.

issues.t: Block heater cord can crack in the cold (recall)
issues.sym: Cracked or split insulation on the engine block heater cord, with bare wires showing.
issues.why: The cord insulation can break down in very cold weather, creating a shock risk. Covered by recall 14V-417.
issues.next: Don't handle the cord while it is plugged in. Have the dealer replace it under the recall.

issues.t: Fuel line can rub the engine and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gas smell under the hood or fuel dripping near the engine.
issues.why: On some 2.0L turbo cars built in early 2016, the fuel line was routed where it can touch the engine and wear through. Covered by recall 16V-595.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't drive; turn the engine off and call for a tow. Check your VIN for the free fuel line replacement.
